description: Given an integer n, return the number of trailing zeroes in n!. Trailing zeroes are produced by factors of 10 = 2 * 5. Since there are always more factors of 2 than 5, count the factors of 5.
intuition: Trailing zeros come from factors of 10, and 10 = 2 x 5. Since there are always more factors of 2 than 5, just count factors of 5. Every multiple of 5 contributes one factor, every multiple of 25 contributes an extra, and so on.
approach: Count the number of factors of 5 in n!. Each multiple of 5 contributes one factor, each multiple of 25 contributes an extra, each multiple of 125 contributes yet another, and so on.
jsWalkthrough:
Input: n = 25

25! = 1 * 2 * 3 * ... * 25

Counting factors of 5:
Iteration 1: n = floor(25/5) = 5, count = 0+5 = 5
  (multiples of 5 up to 25: 5,10,15,20,25 -> five 5-factors)
Iteration 2: n = floor(5/5) = 1, count = 5+1 = 6
  (25 = 5*5 contributes an extra factor of 5)
n=1 < 5, loop ends

Output: 6 (25! ends in 6 zeros)
explanation:
1. Trailing zeros come from factors of 10 = 2 * 5.
2. Factors of 2 are more abundant, so just count factors of 5.
3. n // 5 counts multiples of 5, n // 25 counts multiples of 25, etc.
4. Sum n//5 + n//25 + n//125 + ... until n < 5.
5. This is equivalent to repeatedly dividing n by 5 and summing.
hints: Trailing zeros come from pairs of factors 2 and 5.
There are always more 2s than 5s in n!, so just count the 5s.
Multiples of 25 contribute two 5s, multiples of 125 contribute three, etc.
